MOS-5.title: Run the first MOSAIC reader-comprehension test
MOS-5.description:
## Outcome

Obtain direct evidence of whether first-time readers understand what MOSAIC is, when it is useful, what it produces, and how a worked example demonstrates its principles.

## Why

The current assessment is expert review rather than evidence from real readers. Broad copy or example changes made before observing readers could optimise the wrong problem.

## Scope

* Recruit approximately three people who are unfamiliar with MOSAIC and who make professional decisions with incomplete information.
* Run an unaided first-impression test of the opening proposition.
* Allow five minutes of free exploration, then ask the participant to explain MOSAIC without looking at the site.
* Use one paired worked example: ask the participant to predict what a change will do, observe the result, explain the principle, and transfer it to another situation.
* Ask whether MOSAIC is making the decision or supporting human judgement, how it differs from merely gathering more data, and what should happen when a critical gap is discovered.
* After the unaided baseline, test the candidate outcome-first proposition and questions about the first useful action and tangible result.
* Retain anonymised verbatim answers, navigation choices, hesitation, unfamiliar terms and confident misunderstandings.

## Constraints

* Do not explain MOSAIC before the unaided test.
* Do not require exact recall of the six stage names.
* Do not rewrite the proposition between participants in the initial round.
* Treat comprehension as demonstrated only when the participant explains causality or transfers a principle.
* Separate observed evidence from interpretation and recommendations.

## Verification

* Anonymised notes are added to the existing reader-comprehension project document.
* The evidence shows whether readers can identify the decision context, incomplete evidence, alternatives or uncertainty, justified action, tangible decision record and conditions for reconsideration.
* Findings support an explicit next decision about proposition copy, the complete worked example, or the first useful interaction.

MOS-8.title: Audit MOSAIC’s zero-click discovery surfaces using reader language
MOS-8.description:
## Outcome

Create an evidence-based baseline of how a relevant person currently discovers and understands MOSAIC across search, AI answers, social/community surfaces and the MOSAIC website.

## Why

The supplied zero-click marketing talk argues that first impressions increasingly occur before a website visit. MOSAIC should know what those first impressions are before investing in content or optimisation.

This work is intentionally gated by <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue>. The audit should use the words, questions and misunderstandings observed from real first-time readers rather than invented marketing keywords.

## Scope

* Extract approximately ten high-intent questions from <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> evidence, covering the problem, desired outcome, method, comparison, trust and first useful action.
* Select only the discovery surfaces plausibly used by the people represented in <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue>.
* For each question and surface, record:
  * whether MOSAIC appears;
  * the answer or impression formed without a click;
  * sources cited, quoted or repeated;
  * inaccurate, missing or unsupported claims;
  * the apparent format and community norms;
  * a responsible proof point MOSAIC could publish, if any.
* Distinguish owned, earned and third-party surfaces.
* Identify no more than two channels suitable for a bounded pilot.
* Add findings and recommendations to the zero-click strategy document.

## Constraints

* Research only; do not post, contact communities, solicit reviews or change public copy.
* Do not treat the talk's quantitative claims as verified evidence.
* Do not use generic search-volume lists as a substitute for reader language.
* Do not recommend every platform.
* Do not optimise for AI mentions at the expense of accuracy.
* Preserve screenshots or dated notes where results are volatile.

## Verification

* Ten questions are traceable to observed reader evidence or explicitly marked as hypotheses.
* Each audited surface has a dated observation and source.
* The output states where MOSAIC is absent, misunderstood or unsupported.
* The recommendation selects zero, one or two pilot channels with a clear rationale.
* The audit identifies one validated worked example or proof unit suitable for standalone use, or explicitly concludes that none is ready.

## Reference

[Zero-click discovery and content strategy — implications for MOSAIC](<https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/document/zero-click-discovery-and-content-strategy-implications-for-mosaic-eb2ae37761be>)

MOS-9.title: Run a four-week zero-click discovery pilot for one validated MOSAIC insight
MOS-9.description:
## Outcome

Test whether one validated MOSAIC insight can create understanding, recall and meaningful action when delivered natively on the two most credible discovery surfaces identified by <issue id="3c14dc44-f5f8-4f38-82e5-e3c1b6725e7e" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-8/audit-mosaics-zero-click-discovery-surfaces-using-reader-language">MOS-8</issue>.

## Why

The talk's useful strategic claim is that content must deliver value before a click and that last-click attribution cannot explain the full discovery journey. A short, bounded experiment can test this for MOSAIC without committing to a broad content programme.

## Entry criteria

Do not start until:

* <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> has identified language readers understand and a useful first action;
* <issue id="3c14dc44-f5f8-4f38-82e5-e3c1b6725e7e" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-8/audit-mosaics-zero-click-discovery-surfaces-using-reader-language">MOS-8</issue> has identified no more than two credible surfaces;
* one worked example accurately demonstrates a MOSAIC principle;
* every proposed claim is traceable to source material;
* there is a meaningful, proportionate next action.

If any entry criterion fails, return the issue to Backlog with the missing evidence recorded.

## Scope

* Choose one validated worked example or proof unit.
* Define the internal client, job, audience, moment of use, desired action, source owner, success signal, distribution plan and refresh trigger.
* Create one reusable source brief and adapt it into native formats for no more than two channels.
* Publish one or two standalone value assets per week for four weeks.
* Keep founder and company roles distinct:
  * founder voice for perspective, judgement and lessons;
  * company surface for durable examples, methods and evidence.
* Use approximately five useful value deposits for each direct ask.
* When making an ask, describe the useful result and size of commitment.
* Record self-reported discovery when a meaningful action exists.
* Review learning weekly and evaluate patterns after the full pilot.

## Measurement

Track a simple sequence rather than claiming single-touch attribution:

1. **Audience:** relevant repeat readers, followers or subscribers.
2. **Reach:** qualified impressions, views or attention.
3. **Interest:** thoughtful replies, saves, shares, branded discovery or worked-example use.
4. **Outcome:** research participation, qualified conversations, repeat use, pilot interest or other validated action.

Compare weekly activity with meaningful actions over the following two to four weeks. Record qualitative evidence and confounders. Do not claim causality from correlation alone.

## Constraints

* Do not add more channels during the four-week pilot.
* Do not use mass-generated AI copy, synthetic engagement or forum seeding.
* Do not require a click for the asset to be useful.
* Do not publish claims that outrun MOSAIC's evidence.
* Do not optimise for traffic or follower count as the primary outcome.
* Do not launch a generic newsletter unless a recurring promise has already been validated.
* Use AI only to stress-test clarity, evidence, counterarguments and examples; the final judgement and voice remain human.
* No paid media in this experiment.

## Verification

* The content brief names the internal client, job, audience, source evidence and success signal.
* Every asset is understandable without visiting the website.
* The ratio of value deposits to direct asks is recorded.
* Results include all four measurement layers, qualitative evidence and limitations.
* A final decision is recorded: stop, revise, repeat, or scale.
* Scaling requires repeated qualified engagement or a meaningful downstream action—not reach alone.

## References

* [Zero-click discovery and content strategy — implications for MOSAIC](<https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/document/zero-click-discovery-and-content-strategy-implications-for-mosaic-eb2ae37761be>)
* <issue id="3c14dc44-f5f8-4f38-82e5-e3c1b6725e7e" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-8/audit-mosaics-zero-click-discovery-surfaces-using-reader-language">MOS-8</issue>

MOS-6.title: Handle tied explanations honestly in Structure + Analysis
MOS-6.description:
## Observed

When all three explanations have the same highest independent-signal count, the Structure + Analysis example declares “The release introduced friction” as the current analytical lead. The implementation sorts equal counts and selects the first entry, creating an arbitrary winner.

## Expected

A tie must be represented explicitly. The example should say there is no single analytical lead and identify the jointly supported explanations. It should declare one lead only when that explanation has strictly greater support.

## Evidence / reproduction

1. Open the Structure + Analysis worked example.
2. Include the four default evidence items.
3. Keep the dashboard and weekly email linked as duplicate reports.
4. Observe that Release friction, Unclear positioning and Market change each show one independent signal.
5. Observe that the interface nevertheless declares Release friction the analytical lead.

The current source ranks the counts and uses the first sorted entry without checking whether the highest count is shared.

## Constraints

* Preserve the existing explanation-counting and duplicate-linking lesson.
* Preserve the no-supported-explanation state.
* Do not redesign unrelated worked examples.
* Do not label this a Regression because there is no evidence that the tied state previously worked correctly.

## Verification

* A tied top count produces an explicit no-single-leader result naming the tied explanations.
* A unique top count still produces the correct analytical lead.
* Zero support still produces the existing no-supported-explanation result.
* Add automated coverage for tied, unique-leader and zero-support states.
* Formatting, lint and relevant tests pass.

MOS-3.title: Assess the Codie Sanchez 6M insights for MOSAIC
MOS-3.description:
## Outcome

Review [Codie Sanchez 6M marketing assessment — implications for MOSAIC](<https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/document/codie-sanchez-6m-marketing-assessment-implications-for-mosaic-45c1d58ceeef>) and decide which insights, if any, should influence the active MOSAIC proposition work or later adoption planning.

## Why

The assessment contains potentially useful ideas about outcome-first messaging, micro-commitments, value-based calls to action, audience ownership, and sustained campaigns. They remain external hypotheses rather than verified evidence or agreed strategy.

## Scope

* Assess whether outcome-first positioning should be tested against the current proposition.
* Identify the easiest valuable first "yes" MOSAIC could ask for.
* Decide what tangible result a first interaction should produce.
* Assess whether the current primary calls to action make the value exchange clear.
* Decide whether any later work on audience ownership or a sustained campaign is justified.
* Record a deliberate decision to adopt, test, defer, or reject each material implication.

## Constraints

* Do not imitate artificial scarcity, hype, or manipulative funnel techniques.
* Do not treat claims from the video as verified without reviewing the original source.
* Do not turn the six ideas into six implementation issues.
* Do not create a new project unless the assessment reveals a distinct outcome that cannot live in an existing project.
* Proposition comprehension comes before CTA optimisation.

## Verification

* The decision and reasoning are recorded in the linked document or a concise Linear note.
* Any selected work has a clear existing or explicitly approved project home.
* Deferred or rejected ideas remain context rather than entering the backlog accidentally.

MOS-2.title: Review the MOSAIC Mandala and choose the next 1–3 outcomes
MOS-2.description:
## Outcome

Review [MOSAIC Mandala — strategic map and next-phase hypothesis](<https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/document/mosaic-mandala-strategic-map-and-next-phase-hypothesis-d31c6b339c7b>) and explicitly choose no more than one to three outcomes for the next phase, or decide that no new work should be committed yet.

## Why

The Mandala exposes possible imbalance across methodology, evidence, reasoning, product, demonstrated value, trust, reach, and adoption. Its value comes from helping choose leverage, not from turning 64 cells into tasks.

## Scope

* Validate or revise the centre and eight conditions for success.
* Identify where MOSAIC is currently most unbalanced.
* Evaluate the eight high-leverage candidates.
* Decide whether the next phase should emphasise formalising, demonstrating, or putting MOSAIC in people's hands.
* Decide whether selected work belongs in an existing project or warrants a new project.
* Create implementation issues only after those outcome decisions are explicit.

## Constraints

* The 64 cells are a strategic map, not a backlog.
* Select no more than one to three outcomes.
* Do not create work merely because a cell is interesting.
* Preserve the existing active proposition project and its current commitments unless a deliberate decision changes them.

## Verification

* The review decision is recorded in the Mandala document or a linked planning note.
* Selected outcomes, if any, have a clear project home.
* Non-selected ideas remain uncommitted strategic context.

MOS-4.title: Verify Linear and GitHub connectivity for grounds-to-act-mosaic
MOS-4.description:
## Outcome

Verify that Linear automatically links branch, commit, and pull-request activity from the actively relevant GitHub repository "SimonMGarrett/grounds-to-act-mosaic".

## Why

Phase A of the Linear and Codex workflow requires a proven issue-to-code connection, useful GitHub status automation, and enough repository access to support later Code Intelligence and regression monitoring.

## Scope

* Create a short-lived branch whose name contains this issue identifier.
* Add one removable HTML comment to README.md.
* Commit with this issue identifier.
* Push the branch.
* Create a pull request if an already-authenticated supported route is available.
* Verify which branch, commit, and pull-request records appear automatically in Linear.
* Record any settings that still require manual UI configuration.

## Constraints

* Do not modify production behavior.
* Do not merge or deploy the test change.
* Do not install software or read credentials to create the pull request.
* Keep the change atomic and easy to remove.
* GitHub remains authoritative for branch, commit, pull request, checks, and merge state.

## Verification

* Linear automatically displays the connected GitHub activity, or the missing link is documented precisely.
* Repository checks pass.
* Any remaining GitHub, Diffs, Code Intelligence, or Agent guidance setup is described with its exact UI path.
* The temporary pull request or branch is left unmerged until the connectivity result is reviewed.

MOS-1.title: Reconcile deployed insight images with version-controlled source
MOS-1.description:
## Outcome

The three recently changed insight images, their accessibility text, the deployed site, and the version-controlled source all agree. GitHub is again authoritative for what is live.

## Why

The new imagery is visible in production under the legacy JPG/PNG URLs, but the live alt text still describes the previous images. The local repository instead contains an uncommitted migration to new WebP filenames. This mismatch makes the deployment difficult to reproduce and leaves inaccurate accessibility text live.

## Scope

* Preserve the new images currently visible in production.
* Reconcile all three changed insight assets and source references between production and the repository.
* Correct each image's alt text so it describes the image actually shown.
* Decide explicitly whether to retain stable legacy URLs or complete the WebP-path migration; do not leave both states partially implemented.
* Commit and push the final assets and source, then deploy from that versioned state.

## Constraints

* Do not revert to the previous images.
* Do not make unrelated design or editorial changes.
* Keep GitHub as the authoritative source for deployable code and assets.

## Verification

* Formatting, lint, unit tests, browser tests, and production build pass.
* Each of the three live insight pages renders the intended new image with accurate alt text.
* Each referenced live image URL returns an image content type and loads with non-zero natural dimensions.
* The deployed asset paths and content match the committed source.

comments.body:
## Participant 1 evidence recorded

The first participant understood the overall MOSAIC concept and could present back most of the six stages. The strongest example was Meaning + Observations.

The interaction evidence was less positive:

* Structure + Analysis and Interpretation + Choice were “too wordy”.
* She had to “read a lot to see what had changed” when propositions changed.
* The complete example was clearer, but she felt constrained by predefined choices: “I had to choose from a list that had already been decided.”
* She wanted to express responses the interface did not permit.

The full observation, interpretation and follow-up questions have been added to the project’s reader-comprehension document.

MOS-5 remains open. This is useful directional evidence from one participant, not yet justification for a broad redesign or unrestricted free-form input.

Planning review completed on 17 September 2026. The linked 6M assessment now records which principles are adopted as test hypotheses, the comprehension and value-exchange questions to use in reader testing, the unresolved first valuable yes, the ideas retained for later, the work explicitly deferred, and the manipulative techniques rejected. The external quantitative claims remain unverified and are not being relied upon.

Planning review completed on 17 September 2026. The linked Mandala document now records the adopted working architecture, the diagnosis that Demonstrated Value is the current imbalance, the two selected Cycle 1 outcomes, retained future candidates, explicit non-commitments, and the decision to keep the work in the existing proposition project. The 64 cells remain strategic context, not a backlog.

Phase A completed — 16 Sep 2026

- Code Intelligence is unavailable on the current Linear Basic plan. The SPEC requires it only where available, so this is an accepted plan limitation rather than outstanding work.
- The MOSAIC team agent guidance has been added by Simon.
- Simon configured the GitHub workflow options available on the Basic plan.
- Core connectivity is verified: issue-to-PR linking, Linear Diffs, repository branch and commit flow, and PR checks all worked.
- GitHub PR #1 has now been closed without merging. Its remote test branch remains preserved and production was not changed.

Phase A is complete.

Connectivity is verified: the GitHub PR is linked, mergeable, and checks have completed successfully. The remaining work is enabling Code Intelligence, adding team agent guidance, and configuring the requested status automations.

Phase A connectivity verification — 16 Sep 2026

- Repository: SimonMGarrett/grounds-to-act-mosaic

472c0610-26eb-4063-bb73-5700a6e3ce9a.title: Zero-click discovery and content strategy — implications for MOSAIC
472c0610-26eb-4063-bb73-5700a6e3ce9a.content:
## Status and provenance

Captured on 24 September 2026 from a user-supplied transcript of a talk about zero-click marketing.

The transcript does not include a source URL or a complete bibliography. Quantitative claims about search behaviour, platform reach, attribution, advertising incrementality, email performance and named company results have not been independently verified here. Treat them as directional context, not MOSAIC evidence.

This document translates the useful strategic principles into hypotheses and staged experiments for MOSAIC. It does not approve a broad campaign or create a new project.

## Executive assessment

The talk reinforces a useful shift for MOSAIC:

> Discovery is no longer a reliable journey from a link to a website. MOSAIC must be understandable, credible and memorable on the surfaces where a prospective user first encounters it.

For MOSAIC, this does **not** mean publishing more generic content. It means turning the product’s strongest reasoning patterns, examples and proof into self-contained public evidence that is useful without a click.

The immediate constraint remains unchanged: MOSAIC has not yet completed its first reader-comprehension test or validated its most useful first interaction. Marketing scale before that evidence would amplify an unclear proposition.

Recommended sequence:

1. **Validate the proposition and first useful interaction** through <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue>.
2. **Audit the public discovery surfaces** using the language real readers use.
3. **Run one bounded zero-click pilot** around one validated worked example.
4. **Measure patterns between attention, intent and meaningful action**, not last-click attribution.
5. **Scale only if the pilot creates useful learning or qualified demand.**

## What changes for MOSAIC

### 1. The website is not the only homepage

A prospective user may form their first impression from:

* a search result or snippet;
* an AI-generated answer;
* a founder post;
* a specialist discussion;
* a talk, newsletter or podcast mention;
* a colleague’s recommendation;
* a worked example quoted elsewhere.

The product proposition must therefore survive outside the full website. A short description, worked insight or proof point should still communicate:

* the decision situation;
* why ordinary analysis is insufficient;
* what MOSAIC helps a person do;
* what tangible result remains;
* what MOSAIC does **not** automate or decide.

### 2. The atomic marketing unit should be a useful decision insight

A MOSAIC content unit should deliver standalone value, for example:

* one way to distinguish evidence from inference;
* one example of source dependence changing an analysis;
* one decision-changing unknown;
* one reconsideration trigger;
* one before-and-after decision frame;
* one short decision record showing why an action was reasonable at the time.

These units can be repurposed into a founder post, company archive entry, email note, talk example and fuller website page. The reusable asset is the underlying insight and evidence, not a platform-specific post.

### 3. Public evidence is part of product trust

MOSAIC’s differentiator is defensible reasoning. Important proof should not remain only in private notes or internal discussions. When evidence supports it, MOSAIC should publish:

* transparent worked decisions;
* method definitions;
* traceable sources and assumptions;
* explicit limitations;
* anonymised case evidence;
* revision history or reconsideration conditions.

This helps people and answer engines encounter a more accurate public record. It must not become an attempt to manipulate forums, reviews or AI systems.

### 4. Content should have an internal client and a job

Before creating an asset, record:

 1. Internal client: product research, adoption, user education, trust, sales or another named function.
 2. Job to be done.
 3. Audience and decision context.
 4. Desired asset or native format.
 5. Moment of use.
 6. Desired next action.
 7. Source material and subject-matter owner.
 8. Success signal and target.
 9. Distribution plan.
10. Shelf life and refresh trigger.

If these cannot be answered, the asset is not ready.

Examples:

| Asset | Internal client | Job | Useful success signal |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Worked decision | Product research / adoption | Demonstrate the method and reveal misunderstanding | Readers can explain and transfer the principle |
| Case study | Adoption / sales | Reduce perceived risk with credible proof | Qualified conversations, shorter decision cycle |
| Method note | Trust | Make a claim citable and inspectable | Relevant mentions, references, informed questions |
| How-to guide | User education | Help someone apply one MOSAIC move | Completion, reuse, reduced clarification |
| Founder post | Discovery | Teach one useful idea in the feed | Qualified engagement, branded discovery, subscriber growth |

### 5. Measurement should distinguish attention, interest and outcomes

Traffic is a diagnostic, not the primary success measure.

Use four layers:

| Layer | MOSAIC examples |
| -- | -- |
| Audience | Relevant followers, repeat readers, subscribers, direct participants |
| Reach | Qualified impressions, views, minutes watched or read |
| Interest | Saves, thoughtful replies, shares, branded search, worked-example use |
| Outcome | Reader-test participation, useful feedback, qualified conversations, repeat use, pilot or adoption |

The primary question is not “Which post got the conversion?” It is:

> When MOSAIC increases useful exposure among a defined audience, do meaningful actions and evidence of understanding rise afterwards?

Use a simple monthly correlation view. Retain self-reported discovery (“How did you first hear about MOSAIC?”) when a meaningful action exists. Where volume is sufficient, use bounded channel or timing tests rather than trusting platform attribution.

### 6. Own one durable relationship, but only when the exchange is useful

Email is a plausible owned channel because it preserves a direct relationship. MOSAIC should not add a generic newsletter merely to collect addresses.

A subscription becomes justified when it offers a clear recurring benefit, such as:

* one worked decision pattern;
* one decision-quality diagnostic;
* one annotated case;
* one method improvement or evidence update.

The value exchange must be explicit and proportionate.

### 7. Founder voice and company record have different roles

A working hypothesis from the talk:

* **Founder channel:** perspective, judgement, stories and lessons.
* **Company channel:** stable record of examples, methods, releases and evidence.

The founder voice may earn attention; the company record should preserve durable, citable material. Neither should merely repeat the other.

### 8. AI should stress-test content, not replace MOSAIC’s voice or evidence

Use AI to challenge a finished draft:

* Where is the claim weak?
* Which example is missing?
* What could be misunderstood?
* Which counterargument is strongest?
* What evidence would change the conclusion?

Do not use AI to manufacture generic thought leadership, invented proof or an authoritative voice unsupported by MOSAIC’s work.

## Proposed operating model

### Now: complete validation

* Complete <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> without changing the proposition between initial participants.
* Capture the phrases people naturally use for the problem, desired outcome and tangible result.
* Identify recurring questions, misconceptions and transfer failures.
* Decide which worked example and first action are genuinely useful.

### Next: discovery audit

Using the validated reader language, define approximately ten high-intent questions and inspect the surfaces where a relevant audience may encounter answers.

Record:

* whether MOSAIC appears;
* what answer or impression is currently formed;
* which sources are cited or repeated;
* which claims are inaccurate, absent or unsupported;
* which communities and formats appear genuinely relevant;
* which proof MOSAIC could responsibly publish.

This is research, not reputation management.

### Then: four-week pilot

Choose no more than two channels on evidence, not preference. Publish one or two self-contained assets per week from a single validated worked example.

Suggested constraints:

* one underlying idea per asset;
* native value without requiring a click;
* roughly five value deposits for each direct ask;
* founder and company roles kept distinct;
* one clear, proportionate action when an ask is made;
* every claim traceable to source material;
* no synthetic engagement, forum seeding or mass AI copy.

Review weekly for learning and monthly for patterns. Change channel choice only after the pilot unless evidence shows clear harm or irrelevance.

## Development implications

Do not build a content platform from this talk. Development work becomes justified only where it strengthens the validated experience or makes trustworthy evidence reusable.

Potential later requirements:

* stable URLs for worked decisions and method claims;
* shareable summaries that remain intelligible out of context;
* visible provenance, assumptions, limitations and revision dates;
* structured metadata for accurate search snippets and previews;
* lightweight, privacy-respecting capture of meaningful actions and self-reported discovery;
* reusable representations of a decision insight across website, email and native posts.

These remain hypotheses until <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> and the discovery audit identify a real need.

## Success gates

Proceed from audit to pilot only if:

* <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> produces a proposition and first interaction that readers can explain;
* at least one worked example teaches a principle accurately;
* the audit finds a plausible audience/surface match;
* MOSAIC has a useful standalone insight with source support;
* a meaningful next action exists.

Scale the pilot only if it produces at least one of:

* repeated qualified engagement from the intended audience;
* clearer branded discovery or direct recall;
* subscriber growth tied to a useful recurring promise;
* reader-test or research participation;
* qualified conversations;
* evidence that people can explain or apply a MOSAIC principle.

## Guardrails

* Do not treat traffic, impressions or follower growth as the primary outcome.
* Do not publish on every platform.
* Do not spam Reddit or other communities.
* Do not optimise for answer-engine mentions at the expense of truth.
* Do not create a generic newsletter before a useful recurring promise exists.
* Do not let AI author MOSAIC’s judgement, evidence or voice.
* Do not infer causality from one attribution report or one high-performing post.
* Do not let marketing claims outrun product evidence.
* Do not create a broad launch while the proposition and first experience remain unvalidated.

## Decisions captured

### Adopt now

* Treat reader language from <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> as input to discoverability research.
* Design future assets to deliver standalone value and remain understandable outside the website.
* Preserve public, citable evidence for MOSAIC’s strongest claims.
* Measure attention, interest and outcomes as a sequence rather than demanding single-touch attribution.
* Use AI as a critic and editor, not a substitute author.

### Queue as gated research

* Audit MOSAIC’s discovery surfaces after <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue>.
* Run a bounded zero-click pilot only after the audit identifies a credible audience, channel and proof unit.

### Defer

* Newsletter launch.
* Broad content calendar.
* Employee advocacy programme.
* Paid acquisition tests.
* Major analytics or content-platform development.
* Large-scale search or answer-engine optimisation.

## Relationship to existing MOSAIC strategy

This extends, rather than replaces, the MOSAIC Mandala and the Codie Sanchez assessment.

It supports the same sequence:

> **Formalise it → demonstrate it → put it in people’s hands.**

The new contribution is an operating model for the final movement: put a validated idea in front of people in a form that creates understanding even when no click occurs.

## Status and authority

This is a source register derived from pre-MOSAIC notes in `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS`.

It is not a MOSAIC architecture, requirements document or backlog. Current MOSAIC decisions, implemented behaviour and Linear planning take precedence. Technologies named here are historical options, not selections.

## Potentially useful technical threads

### Accept messy inputs without pretending they are clean

Several notes assume that useful work begins with inconsistent files, mixed formats, missing values and disconnected sources. They explore conversion, schema discovery, profiling, normalisation, sampling and data-quality checks.

This supports the current MOSAIC hypothesis that evidence intake should tolerate messy and unstructured material while preserving what was supplied. It does not imply that MOSAIC should become a general ETL platform.

Historical sources include:

* `002 - IDEAS/Conversion, mapping, and LuckAlb_.md`
* `002 - IDEAS/Lakehouse - Ideas, Spec, How to.md`
* `003 - PROJECT DEVELOPMENT/QUIRKY GERBIL/_Initial_Specification.md`
* `003 - PROJECT DEVELOPMENT/QUIRKY GERBIL/Converting Messy Data into Actionable Visualisations.md`
* `004 - TECH and DATA/Using DuckDB for conversion.md`
* `004 - TECH and DATA/Tooling Outline.md`

### Separate conversion, understanding and interpretation

The Quirky Gerbil material distinguishes converting data into a usable form from understanding its structure and then presenting it meaningfully.

That separation is compatible with MOSAIC's stronger distinction between evidence, inference and judgement. The old component names and designs should not be adopted directly.

### Preserve relationships, identity and provenance

Historical work on entity extraction, record linkage, graphs and source enrichment may later help MOSAIC represent:

* when records refer to the same entity;
* relationships between evidence items;
* source dependence and duplication;
* traceability to original material;
* context gathered from additional sources.

Relevant sources include:

* `S and B - Record Linkage System.md`
* `004 - TECH and DATA/SpaCy Stuff.md`
* `002 - IDEAS/Research for ML Work.md`
* `003 - PROJECT DEVELOPMENT/Info from old newspapers.md`
* `002 - IDEAS/_MY INNOVATIONS.md`

These are implementation possibilities, not a decision that MOSAIC requires a knowledge graph or a particular entity-resolution library.

### Make uncertainty and model behaviour inspectable

The anomaly-detection, HMM and analytical notes favour explicit features, transparent scoring and visible uncertainty rather than unexplained conclusions.

That instinct is compatible with MOSAIC, but the specific statistical methods belong to particular analytical use cases, not the core MOSAIC method.

Sources include:

* `003 - PROJECT DEVELOPMENT/AIS HMM.md`
* `700 - RESEARCH/_OUTLINE.md`
* `004 - TECH and DATA/Monte Carlo Models.md`

### Prefer observable behaviour over declared design

The note `Understanding Complex Systems.md` suggests examining actual exchanges between system components rather than trusting specifications alone.

For MOSAIC, this may be useful as a general evidence principle: distinguish claimed behaviour from observed behaviour. It is a candidate insight, not an adopted rule.

### Visualisation should support reasoning, not merely presentation

The older material repeatedly treats visualisation as a way to reveal patterns, relationships and context. A MOSAIC interface should only adopt these ideas where they help users inspect evidence, alternatives, uncertainty and decision consequences.

The old dashboard, Streamlit, Power BI and graph-interface choices are not current product decisions.

### Local, offline and constrained deployment

Notes on local language models, air-gapped ClickHouse and private tooling show an enduring concern for restricted environments.

This is compatible with the Mandala's future privacy and deployment-options thread. It does not justify current infrastructure work.

Sources include:

* `004 - TECH and DATA/LM Studio.md`
* `ClickHouse.md`
* parts of `_PLANNING/Business Plan.md`

### Security and supply-chain integrity

The archived Trivy article and security notes reinforce that a trustworthy decision system depends on its software supply chain and operational environment. This belongs in future threat modelling and deployment assurance, not the current proposition cycle.

Sources include:

* `Widely used Trivy scanner compromised.md`
* `004 - TECH and DATA/Temp sec stuff.md`
* `600 - SECURITY/Defence Attitude.md`

## Ideas explicitly not promoted

This review does not select:

* ClickHouse, DuckDB, NocoDB, Mage, Streamlit, Power BI or any other named stack;
* a lakehouse or knowledge graph as mandatory architecture;
* blockchain as a proof-of-deletion mechanism;
* a general analyst operating system;
* a generic data-conversion product;
* AIS anomaly detection as core MOSAIC functionality;
* autonomous source gathering or web scraping;
* a particular scoring, clustering or entity-resolution technique.

## Possible later questions

Only revisit these when current MOSAIC evidence makes them relevant:

1. What is the smallest evidence-ingestion capability needed for a real decision?
2. Which provenance and dependence relationships must be represented explicitly?
3. What can run locally or offline without damaging usability?
4. What visual form best exposes reasoning rather than concealing it?
5. Which technical claims require threat modelling or independent verification?

## Effect on current planning

No initiative, project or issue is created from this register. Current Cycle 1 remains unchanged.

5a97572d-8591-4647-94bd-9d4898c00582.title: Pre-MOSAIC Sheridan & Bairns material — relevance assessment
5a97572d-8591-4647-94bd-9d4898c00582.content:
## Status and authority

This document assesses planning material in the Obsidian area `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS`. The source notes pre-date MOSAIC.

They are historical inputs, not MOSAIC requirements, decisions or backlog. Current MOSAIC decisions, terminology, methodology, Linear planning, and implemented behaviour take precedence whenever there is a conflict.

The current authoritative planning context is the **MOSAIC Adoption** initiative, the **MOSAIC Mandala — strategic map and next-phase hypothesis**, and the active project **Make the MOSAIC proposition clear and convincing**.

## Why retain this assessment

The historical material contains ideas that independently converge with parts of current MOSAIC thinking. Those ideas may strengthen later reasoning, positioning or commercial exploration, but must pass through current MOSAIC evidence and decision processes before becoming commitments.

## Compatible historical threads

### Decisions under costly uncertainty

The clearest recurring historical proposition is helping organisations make sense of complex, risky and fragmented information where blind spots are expensive.

This is compatible with MOSAIC's current centre:

> MOSAIC becomes a credible, useful and adopted system for making defensible decisions under uncertainty.

The historical phrasing is useful as candidate audience language, not approved MOSAIC copy.

### Decision support, not decision ownership

The old business-planning material distinguishes analysis and decision support from legal, compliance or operational sign-off. It argues that the client or human decision-maker retains responsibility.

This reinforces current MOSAIC commitments to human agency, explicit judgement and defensibility. It does not add a new requirement.

### Epistemic discipline

The historical notes repeatedly emphasise:

* what is known and unknown;
* incomplete data and blind spots;
* confidence and uncertainty signalling;
* alternative explanations;
* explicit scope and intended use;
* language that avoids claiming certainty.

These themes are already represented more rigorously in the current Mandala under **Evidence & knowledge**, **Uncertainty & reasoning**, and **Trust & defensibility**. The current MOSAIC formulation is authoritative.

### Messy inputs

Several old notes assume users begin with disconnected spreadsheets, documents, emails or datasets rather than a clean model.

This supports the existing future MOSAIC candidate of accepting messy and unstructured inputs while retaining provenance and traceability. It does not justify implementation work during the current cycle.

### Real-user validation

The historical company plans repeatedly say that ideas should meet real people before substantial execution, and suggest a small number of deep conversations with aligned organisations.

This is consistent with the active reader-comprehension work and the Mandala's later adoption hypotheses. Current reader evidence should come first; the legacy material does not justify a new commercial-validation project now.

### Candidate audiences

Historical audience hypotheses include people responsible for risk, compliance, intelligence or insight, strategy, national infrastructure and other settings where uncertainty is consequential.

These remain unvalidated candidates. MOSAIC should not adopt them as its target market without current evidence.

### Safe future engagement

If MOSAIC later supports a commercial service or pilot, the old notes contain useful reminders to define:

* the question being addressed;
* included and excluded evidence;
* intended use of outputs;
* known limitations and uncertainty;
* what remains a human, legal, compliance or operational judgement.

These are future design inputs, not legal guidance and not committed work.

## Historical ideas not promoted into MOSAIC

The following remain outside the current MOSAIC plan:

* particular consultancy packages or prices;
* data-cleaning, knowledge-graph, private-AI and OSINT product concepts;
* lead magnets, funnels and campaign tactics;
* proposed organisation and hiring structures;
* website aesthetics and legacy Sheridan & Bairns service language;
* unverified market-size estimates;
* legacy project codenames and product ideas.

They may still matter to Sheridan & Bairns independently, but must not be mistaken for MOSAIC strategy.

## Effect on current planning

This review creates no new initiative, project or issue.

It does not change Cycle 1. The current focus remains:

1. obtain evidence from first-time readers;
2. represent tied explanations honestly in the Structure + Analysis example;
3. use the resulting evidence to decide whether to change the proposition, the complete-decision example, or the first useful interaction.

The historical material should be revisited only when a current MOSAIC decision makes one of its hypotheses relevant.

## Obsidian sources reviewed

* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/_PLANNING/01 - Company Purpose.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/_PLANNING/Business Plan.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/_PLANNING/Core SMJG Planning.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/Understanding Complex Systems.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/_PLANNING/dLLM Assessment of Market.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/001 - BD/Products - How to Do Lead Magnets Right.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/002 - IDEAS/How to use Vercel V0.md`
* `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS/003 - PROJECT DEVELOPMENT/_Outline of Projects.md`

## Provenance caution

Several notes contain AI-generated assessments, summaries of uncaptured videos, or unattributed market claims. They should not be treated as verified evidence without reviewing the original sources.

## Corpus-wide extension — 20 September 2026

The remaining pre-MOSAIC Sheridan & Bairns corpus was reviewed after this initial assessment. Useful material has been distilled into two additional historical source registers:

* [Pre-MOSAIC technical and product hypotheses — source register](<https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/document/pre-mosaic-technical-and-product-hypotheses-source-register-614be3a7d46a>)
* [Pre-MOSAIC use cases, audiences and adoption hypotheses — source register](<https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/document/pre-mosaic-use-cases-audiences-and-adoption-hypotheses-source-register-3b22a31340e6>)

All Markdown notes in `003 - SHERIDANandBAIRNS` are now treated as an archived historical corpus. The review created no project or issue because current MOSAIC planning does not justify additional committed work.

f251ef7b-b755-401d-9b2f-2655df9d5128.title: Codie Sanchez 6M marketing assessment — implications for MOSAIC
f251ef7b-b755-401d-9b2f-2655df9d5128.content:
# Codie Sanchez 6M marketing assessment

## Status and provenance

Captured on 16 September 2026 from a GPT-assisted assessment of a Codie Sanchez video.

The video title, URL, and original transcript have not been captured here. This document therefore records the supplied interpretation rather than a verified source analysis. Quantitative or experimental claims attributed to Sanchez — including spend, conversion results, customer-acquisition economics, views, registrations, and time-limited availability — should be treated as unverified unless the original source and supporting evidence are reviewed.

This is external inspiration for reflection, not an agreed MOSAIC strategy or backlog.

## Overall assessment

The substance appears better than the packaging. Beneath the scarcity and "million-dollar secret" framing is a coherent playbook for moving from attention to customers and then to a repeatable sales system.

The underlying sequence is:

**Get attention → make the message resonate → obtain a small commitment → make a clear ask → make the economics work → orchestrate a sustained campaign**

The video also appears to use the techniques while explaining them: scarcity, exclusivity, a free giveaway, repeated calls to action, micro-commitments, customer-centred benefits, a large prize, and the book launch woven throughout. The tutorial is itself part of the funnel.

## The 6M framework

The supplied assessment describes six elements. The first "M" was not explicitly named in the supplied transcript, so its label below is descriptive rather than canonical.

### 1. Attract attention with something people value

Mechanisms described include:

* exclusivity;
* direct self-reference to a recognisable person or problem;
* reciprocity through useful value before an ask;
* concrete, specific giveaways rather than vague "free training";
* delivering value before the desired action, rather than disguising a transaction.

General principle:

> Do not merely promise value. Demonstrate some of the value before asking for commitment.

#### MOSAIC implication

MOSAIC should let people experience useful reasoning before asking them to adopt a framework, start a commercial conversation, or trust a larger product claim. A genuinely useful example or small tool can be both value and explanation.

### 2. Message: the customer is Luke; MOSAIC is Yoda

The customer is the protagonist. The product, company, or framework is the mechanism or guide.

Rule:

**Ideal state first → mechanism second**

Lead with the change a person wants, then explain how MOSAIC helps produce it. Do not lead with structured evidence, knowledge graphs, uncertainty models, AI architecture, or decision traceability simply because those mechanisms are technically interesting.

Candidate outcome-led language:

> **Make important decisions you can understand, explain and defend.**

#### MOSAIC implication

This is directly relevant to the active project **Make the MOSAIC proposition clear and convincing**. The proposition should first communicate the reader's desired outcome and recognisable decision problem. The framework and six stages can then explain the mechanism.

This is a hypothesis to test with readers, not approved replacement copy.

### 3. Micro-commitment: get the first valuable yes

Do not ask a stranger immediately for the largest commitment. Find the easiest valuable action that reduces friction and teaches something about genuine intent.

The source journey was described as:

**free registration → small paid upgrade → larger commercial relationship**

A possible MOSAIC journey is:

**read an article → try a free tool → analyse one decision → save or share the result → use MOSAIC seriously**

#### MOSAIC implication

The current website should not jump conceptually from "interesting framework" to enterprise-scale adoption. It should reveal a useful, proportionate next step.

The strategically important question is:

> What is the easiest valuable yes somebody can give MOSAIC?

Possible answers require validation. They might include trying one worked example, framing one decision, or receiving a useful decision record.

### 4. Make the ask: clarity beats brevity

Very short calls to action such as "Learn more", "Click here", or "Subscribe" may conceal rather than reduce friction.

A good call to action should clarify:

* why the reader should care;
* what they receive;
* what action to take;
* how large the commitment is;
* why the exchange is worthwhile.

Additional principles from the supplied assessment:

* use one primary call to action consistently;
* use a strong, explicit verb;
* make the benefit personal;
* keep the ask proportionate to the relationship;
* frame it as an exchange of value rather than a favour to the organisation.

General principle:

> **Clarity beats brevity.**

#### MOSAIC implication

The proposition project should assess whether each primary call to action describes a meaningful exchange. "Explore the framework" and "Try a worked example" are clear actions, but the reader may still need to know what useful result they will obtain.

CTA testing should follow proposition comprehension, not substitute for it.

### 5. Money: own the customer relationship

The broader principle is that revenue alone does not make a good business. Protect margin, understand acquisition economics, and retain a direct relationship with the audience or customer.

The supplied account emphasises:

* direct communication;
* customer data and distribution control;
* gross margin relative to customer-acquisition cost;
* turning a launch into reusable evergreen material rather than accepting a single spike followed by collapse.

Sequence:

**launch → acquire audience → make an offer → learn what works → turn it into evergreen material → continue**

#### MOSAIC implication

This is more relevant to future adoption and sustainability than to the immediate proposition work. MOSAIC should eventually avoid dependence on channels that obscure who is receiving value and why. However, detailed unit economics would be premature before a validated useful offer and evidence of actual demand.

### 6. Map: orchestrate a campaign

A launch is described as a coordinated sequence of exposures rather than one announcement. Frequency and explicitness increase over time while visual motifs, stories, examples, and ordinary content create familiarity.

General principle:

> A launch is not a post. It is a sustained, coherent sequence that gradually makes the idea familiar.

#### MOSAIC implication

When MOSAIC has something sufficiently useful to launch, promotion should combine essays, examples, demonstrations, tools, and repeated ideas into a coherent world. Grounds to Act, decision records, fragmented evidence, and defensible action already provide potentially distinctive narrative material.

The language of subliminal triggers, artificial scarcity, disappearing content, and activation colours is not something MOSAIC should copy. It conflicts with the existing principles of trust, explicit reasoning, and no dark patterns.

## What is worth retaining

Stripped of the theatrical packaging:

1. Give people something genuinely useful before demanding anything.
2. Talk about the customer's desired outcome, not primarily about the organisation or technology.
3. Design a ladder of increasingly meaningful commitments.
4. Make the next action unmistakably clear and explain its value.
5. Own the audience relationship and understand the economics.
6. Treat promotion as a sustained, coherent campaign rather than one announcement.

## Relevance to MOSAIC now

The most immediately relevant ideas are **Message, Micro-commitment, and Make the ask**.

They bear directly on the current gap between:

> This is an interesting framework.

and:

> I understand why and when I would use this, what I will get, and what I should do next.

They should be treated as hypotheses for the active proposition and reader-comprehension work:

* Can readers state the desired outcome before they know the mechanics?
* Can they identify a useful first action?
* Do they understand what they receive by taking it?
* Does the next step feel proportionate to their current trust and interest?

## Relationship to the MOSAIC Mandala

This assessment intersects four Mandala conditions:

* **Demonstrated value:** give useful value before asking for commitment.
* **Compelling product:** create a meaningful first experience and visible result.
* **Reach & market:** sharpen positioning, free tools, essays, and coherent campaigns.
* **Adoption & sustainability:** create a commitment ladder and retain a direct learning relationship with users.

It reinforces the Mandala hypothesis:

> **Formalise it → demonstrate it → put it in people's hands.**

It does not by itself justify a new project.

## Guardrails

* Do not imitate manipulative scarcity or hype.
* Do not treat marketing claims as verified evidence without the original source.
* Do not optimise calls to action before the proposition is understandable.
* Do not construct a commercial funnel before there is a genuinely useful first experience.
* Do not turn the six ideas into six issues automatically.
* Preserve human agency and make the exchange explicit.

## Possible later decisions

These are questions for planning, not committed tasks:

1. Test outcome-first proposition language against the current wording.
2. Define the easiest valuable first "yes" for MOSAIC.
3. Decide what tangible result a first interaction should produce.
4. Test whether the primary CTA makes that exchange clear.
5. Later, decide whether a sustained content and demonstration campaign is justified by a validated offer.

## Planning decision — 17 September 2026

### Adopt now as test principles

* Lead with the reader’s desired outcome and recognisable decision problem; explain MOSAIC as the mechanism afterwards.
* Give a person something genuinely useful before asking for greater commitment.
* Make the value exchange and tangible result explicit.
* Preserve human agency, trust and transparent reasoning.
* Treat specific proposition wording as a hypothesis to test, not approved replacement copy.
* Establish proposition comprehension before optimising calls to action.

The initial reader test should therefore examine whether a first-time reader can identify the desired outcome, when MOSAIC is useful, what tangible result it produces, what useful first action is available, and whether that action feels proportionate to their current understanding and trust.

### Retain as open questions

The easiest valuable first “yes” has not yet been selected. Candidates include trying a worked example, framing one real decision, or receiving a useful decision record. Reader evidence should inform that choice.

A commitment ladder, direct audience relationship, free tool, reusable example packs, acquisition economics and a sustained content or launch campaign remain potentially valuable later. They require a validated useful first experience and evidence of demand.

### Defer

Defer CTA optimisation, funnel design, audience ownership, campaign orchestration, unit economics and launch planning until readers understand MOSAIC and a useful first interaction has been validated.

### Reject

Reject artificial scarcity, hype, subliminal framing, disappearing-content tactics and other dark patterns. Do not treat the uncaptured video’s quantitative claims as evidence. The source claims remain unverified; source verification is unnecessary for the current plan because these ideas are being treated only as hypotheses for testing.

This assessment does not justify a new project or six implementation issues.

b96ec960-4e1a-4321-ab18-db80e3e1de2e.title: MOSAIC Mandala — strategic map and next-phase hypothesis
b96ec960-4e1a-4321-ab18-db80e3e1de2e.content:
# MOSAIC Mandala

## Status and intent

This strategic map was developed by applying Mandala goal setting to MOSAIC and captured on 16 September 2026. It is a hypothesis for later review, not an agreed roadmap.

The eight inner boxes are conditions for success, not departments or arbitrary categories. The 64 second-level cells are the map, not the backlog.

## Centre

**MOSAIC becomes a credible, useful and adopted system for making defensible decisions under uncertainty.**

## First ring: eight conditions for success

1. Rigorous methodology
2. Evidence & knowledge
3. Uncertainty & reasoning
4. Compelling product
5. Demonstrated value
6. Trust & defensibility
7. Reach & market
8. Adoption & sustainability

Each is a potential failure condition: MOSAIC could have excellent software without proof of value, a strong methodology without reach, interest without a trustworthy audit trail, or demonstrations without sustained adoption.

## 1. Rigorous methodology

Aim: make MOSAIC more than a collection of sensible prompts.

* Define exactly what a decision is
* Formalise the six-stage process
* Define stage entry and exit criteria
* Separate evidence, inference and judgement
* Model assumptions explicitly
* Define how decisions are revised
* Document failure modes
* Publish the underlying framework

**Potential intellectual signature:** evidence is not inference, and inference is not judgement.

## 2. Evidence & knowledge

This corresponds closely to the analytical layer.

* Capture provenance
* Represent evidence relationships
* Accept messy and unstructured inputs
* Identify missing evidence
* Detect contradictions
* Represent source characteristics
* Support knowledge graphs
* Preserve traceability to originals

MOSAIC should not require perfect input. It should be good at saying:

> Here is what you actually know, here is why you think you know it, and here is what you do not know.

## 3. Uncertainty & reasoning

Uncertainty should be a first-class pillar rather than disappear inside the evidence model.

* Represent multiple uncertainty types
* Avoid false numerical precision
* Handle conflicting evidence
* Expose assumptions
* Compare plausible interpretations
* Model evidence dimensions
* Show sensitivity to uncertainty
* Identify decision-changing unknowns

The evidence-space idea **E = (o, s, a, r, c, d)** belongs here.

A potentially defining question is:

> Which uncertainty, if resolved, has the greatest chance of changing the decision?

This turns uncertainty into something actionable rather than merely acknowledged.

## 4. Compelling product

The framework must become something people enjoy and value using.

* Excellent decision intake
* Guided evidence exploration
* Clear visual decision workspace
* Useful AI assistance
* Human remains in control
* Excellent reasoning trace
* Action hand-off
* Iterative decision review

Avoid making the first version an enormous enterprise application.

The intended magic moment is:

> I came in thinking the question was X. MOSAIC helped me realise the real question was Y, showed me what I was assuming, and revealed that Z was the thing I actually needed to find out.

## 5. Demonstrated value

This may be the most important near-term quadrant.

* Tiny understandable example
* Rich realistic example
* Messy-data example
* Before and after comparison
* Interactive website demonstration
* Real user case study
* Compare with normal LLM use
* Publish reusable example packs

Current hypothesis: MOSAIC needs proof through examples more than additional theory.

A strong set could span:

* Everyday: Should I move house?
* Professional: Should we adopt technology X?
* Analytical or intelligence: Given incomplete and conflicting evidence, what action is justified?

If the same framework visibly improves all three, MOSAIC becomes understandable as a general decision-management approach rather than another AI application.

## 6. Trust & defensibility

This is a substantial point of distinction from asking an LLM what to do.

* Every claim traceable
* Assumptions visible
* Human judgement identified
* Alternatives preserved
* Changes recorded
* Privacy and deployment options
* Reproducible reasoning
* Explicit limitations

Potential promise:

> MOSAIC does not merely tell you what decision was made. It preserves the grounds on which it was reasonable to make it.

This aligns with Grounds to Act.

A good outcome is not the same thing as a good decision. A well-made decision can produce a bad outcome because the world is uncertain. MOSAIC should preserve why the choice was reasonable given the evidence available at the time.

## 7. Reach & market

People need to discover the idea and immediately understand why they care.

* Sharp positioning
* Excellent website
* Publish distinctive essays
* Useful free tools
* Talks and demonstrations
* Build a practitioner community
* Reach specific professions
* Partnerships and integrations

A useful standalone tool may teach MOSAIC more effectively than an invitation to read about the framework.

Candidate: **Decision Framer**. A user enters a question such as "Should we replace system X?" and receives a structured decision definition, assumptions, stakeholders, uncertainties, and missing evidence. It should be useful independently while teaching how MOSAIC thinks.

## 8. Adoption & sustainability

MOSAIC must survive contact with real organisations and real people.

* Identify strongest initial users
* Conduct user interviews
* Run real pilots
* Make onboarding easy
* Define value and success measures
* Establish a commercial model
* Learn from decision outcomes
* Feed learning back into MOSAIC

The eventual learning loop is:

**Evidence → Decision → Action → Outcome → Learning → Better future decisions**

This would make MOSAIC a decision-learning system rather than a static framework.

## Complete architecture

### Input

Evidence & Knowledge
↓
Uncertainty & Reasoning

### Decision

Rigorous Methodology
↓
Compelling Product
↓
Trust & Defensibility

### Action and learning

Decision → Action → Outcome → Learning

### Surrounding adoption system

Demonstrated Value → Reach → Adoption

This is coherent with the Analytical → Decision → Action model.

## The map is not the backlog

Do not create 64 tasks.

Eight high-leverage candidates for later evaluation are:

1. Formalise exactly what MOSAIC means by a decision.
2. Separate evidence, inference, assumption and judgement.
3. Define the decision-changing unknowns concept.
4. Create one exceptionally good realistic worked example.
5. Build one small free MOSAIC tool.
6. Demonstrate complete traceability from decision back to evidence.
7. Sharpen the one-sentence explanation of MOSAIC.
8. Put MOSAIC in front of real users and observe what happens.

The next phase may reduce to three movements:

> **Formalise it → demonstrate it → put it in people's hands.**

The working diagnosis is that additional conceptual exploration may now have diminishing returns. One excellent worked decision and a small usable tool may reveal more about what MOSAIC needs next than further framework writing.

## Questions for review

* Are these eight conditions genuinely necessary and collectively sufficient?
* Where is MOSAIC currently most unbalanced?
* Which one to three outcomes would generate the most learning now?
* Which candidates belong inside existing projects?
* Does any candidate justify a new project?
* What should explicitly remain uncommitted?

Do not translate the Mandala into projects or issues until those decisions are made.

## Planning decision — 17 September 2026

### Status of the map

The centre and eight conditions are accepted as a useful working architecture for planning, not as a proven or final decomposition. The Mandala remains strategic context rather than a roadmap or backlog.

### Current diagnosis

**Demonstrated Value is the clearest present imbalance.** MOSAIC already has substantial conceptual material, but there is no evidence yet from real first-time readers and parts of the worked examples do not fully demonstrate the principles they claim to teach.

Methodological integrity, trust and defensibility remain constraints on every demonstration. In particular, MOSAIC must keep evidence, inference, assumptions and judgement distinguishable; avoid false numerical precision; preserve human agency; and show what information could change a decision.

### Cycle 1 outcomes

1. Put the current proposition and a worked example in front of first-time readers and retain evidence of comprehension, misunderstanding and transfer.
2. Correct the Structure + Analysis example so tied explanations are represented honestly rather than declaring an arbitrary analytical lead.

Both outcomes belong in the existing project **Make the MOSAIC proposition clear and convincing**. No new project is justified.

### Retained future outcomes

The following remain valuable strategic candidates, but are not committed Cycle 1 work:

* formalise MOSAIC’s definition of a decision;
* sharpen the separation of evidence, inference, assumption and judgement;
* define and test the decision-changing unknowns concept;
* create one exceptionally strong complete worked decision;
* demonstrate end-to-end traceability from evidence to decision;
* determine the most useful first interaction and tangible output;
* consider a small Decision Framer only if evidence supports it as that first interaction;
* expand testing across everyday, professional and analytical contexts;
* eventually close the evidence-to-outcome learning loop.

The next likely decision is whether reader evidence warrants proposition changes, a redesign of the complete-decision example, or a different first interaction.

### Explicit non-commitments

Do not create 64 issues, build an enterprise-scale product, create a new project, or commit the free-tool, campaign, community, partnership, commercial-model or broad framework-formalisation work merely because it appears in the map.

# Reader comprehension and worked-example assessment

## Purpose

Assess whether the current website makes the MOSAIC proposition clear and convincing, beyond reading age alone, and whether the worked examples accurately teach MOSAIC principles.

## Evidence status

This document began as an expert review of the live website and source as at 15 September 2026. Initial evidence from one first-time reader was added on 24 September 2026. One participant is a useful directional signal, not a completed study or sufficient evidence for a redesign.

No completed multi-participant reader-comprehension study or runnable research protocol was found in the repository. The existing website specification contains six success questions, but does not define the participant journey, acceptable answers, evidence capture, or how to distinguish understanding from repetition.

## Overall finding

The site communicates the central problem well: MOSAIC supports decisions when evidence is incomplete or fragmented. It explains MOSAIC values such as traceability, visible uncertainty, alternatives, and defensibility more strongly than it explains the practical mechanism.

A first-time reader may still be unclear about:

* who should use MOSAIC and in which situations;
* what someone actually does when applying it;
* the tangible output, especially the decision record;
* why the method is more useful than ordinary good decision-making;
* how the six stages work together iteratively.

## Readability

A rough Flesch-based calculation on the live text produced approximate US grade levels of:

* Homepage: grade 12
* Framework: grade 13
* Worked-examples index: grade 10
* Meaning + Observations: grade 10
* Structure + Analysis: grade 15
* Interpretation + Choice: grade 13

These are directional heuristics, especially on pages containing interface labels. The pattern nevertheless indicates a relatively demanding reading level. Terms such as provenance, corroboration, possibilistic, decision-sensitive, ordinal comparison, and supportable choice increase the burden.

The homepage contains about 750 words and the framework about 1,060. At an ordinary reading pace these take approximately four and five minutes respectively, before a reader tries an example. The five-minute success condition therefore needs a defined route and exposure.

## Proposition copy

### What works

* "Make strong decisions from fragmented evidence" is concise and memorable.
* The analysis to decision to action model gives MOSAIC a recognisable place in a workflow.
* The copy consistently avoids promising certainty.
* "A decision record that can be revisited" is the most tangible expression of the output.
* The distinction between collecting more information and deciding what could change the choice is compelling.

### What weakens comprehension

* The hero does not identify the intended user or a recognisable moment when MOSAIC should be used.
* Reasoned, defensible, traceable, and supportable recur without immediately demonstrating what makes the resulting decision better.
* The tangible output, a decision record, appears relatively late.
* "Analysis can establish what is true" is stronger than the rest of the framework supports; elsewhere the site more accurately says what may be true.
* The framework page is thorough but functions more as reference material than as a first-time explanation.
* There is no single plain-language sentence describing the end-to-end movement through the six stages.

A candidate proposition for testing is:

"When an important decision cannot wait for perfect information, MOSAIC helps you define the choice, organise the evidence, test competing interpretations, and record why a particular action is justified — and what might change it."

## Worked-example assessment

### Meaning + Observations

Partly successful. Deadline and reversibility clearly change the decision framing, and evidence types remain visible. However, adding a rumour or reported judgement changes only the item count; it does not visibly affect relevance or subsequent reasoning. The claimed lesson is stronger than the demonstrated behaviour.

### Structure + Analysis

The strongest individual teaching example. Linking duplicate reports makes source dependence tangible. However, when all three explanations have one independent signal, the interface still declares the release explanation the analytical lead. This arbitrary tie-break undermines the lesson about disciplined analysis.

### Interpretation + Choice

Strong. It demonstrates that unchanged findings can support different choices when consequences and constraints change. Residual uncertainty and reconsideration triggers reinforce MOSAIC well. The label "assumptions" is loose: supplier qualification is closer to an unresolved fact, while switching cost is a constraint.

### Complete decision

The weakest representation of MOSAIC despite being the most ambitious. The live record and six-stage navigation are useful, but the outcome comes from an undisclosed point calculation. Evidence is reduced to supporting accept or stay; provenance, dependence, contradictions, alternative explanations, gaps, and rejected choices largely disappear. This risks teaching that MOSAIC is a weighted scoring calculator.

Across the examples, iteration and targeted inquiry are not sufficiently demonstrated.

## Assessment of the existing success questions

The existing six questions are useful intent but not a runnable comprehension test.

* Asking for the major stages tests recall more than understanding.
* Asking what one experiment reveals permits a vague answer and tests only one example.
* Asking why Simon might be useful to speak with measures credibility or conversion rather than MOSAIC comprehension.
* The questions do not test intended user, tangible output, iteration, decision ownership, or when more evidence is worthwhile.
* They do not require transfer of a principle to a new situation.

## Recommended reader test

Use a short moderated session with representatives of the intended audiences. Do not explain MOSAIC beforehand.

### 1. First impression

Briefly show the opening section, then hide it. Ask:

* What do you think MOSAIC is?
* When might someone use it?
* What would they have at the end that they did not have before?

### 2. Five-minute exploration

Allow free navigation. Ask the participant to explain MOSAIC to a colleague without looking at the site.

Listen for decision context, incomplete evidence, alternatives or uncertainty, a justified action, and conditions for reconsideration. Do not require exact stage names.

### 3. Worked-example comprehension

Give the participant one paired example. Before changing a control, ask what they expect to happen and why. Afterwards ask:

* What changed?
* Why did it change?
* Which MOSAIC principle did that demonstrate?
* Where might the same principle apply in a different situation?

### 4. Method integrity

Ask:

* Is MOSAIC making the decision or helping a person make it?
* How is it different from gathering more data?
* What should happen when a critical gap or weak assumption is discovered?

## Evidence to retain

Record verbatim answers, navigation choices, hesitation, unfamiliar terms, and confident misunderstandings. Treat comprehension as demonstrated only when a reader can explain causality and transfer the principle, not when they repeat wording from the page.

## Initial reader evidence — participant 1 — 24 September 2026

### Session context

The participant explored the MOSAIC website and was then asked to give a short presentation back to Simon explaining what she understood. The available account does not include timed navigation, verbatim answers beyond the quotations below, participant background, or a full record against every question in the proposed protocol.

### Observed

* She understood the overall MOSAIC concept without much difficulty.
* In the presentation-back exercise, she recovered most of the six stages. This suggests that the framework itself was substantially comprehensible to this participant.
* The **Meaning + Observations** example made the most sense to her.
* She described both **Structure + Analysis** and **Interpretation + Choice** as “too wordy”.
* When a proposition changed in those paired examples, she had to “read a lot to see what had changed”.
* The complete worked example was better than the two wordier paired examples.
* The complete example nevertheless constrained her response. She said: “I had to choose from a list that had already been decided.”
* She wanted to say things that the available choices did not permit.

### Interpretation

These observations separate two problems that should not be conflated:

1. **Framework comprehension:** this participant could understand and recount most of MOSAIC.
2. **Worked-example interaction quality:** several examples imposed excessive comparison effort or insufficient freedom of expression.

The paired examples may be making the reader rediscover changes through repeated reading rather than making the consequential difference visible. The complete example may demonstrate a predetermined decision path more than it demonstrates how MOSAIC helps a person structure their own judgement.

“Total freedom” is not yet established as the correct solution. Useful possibilities to test later include:

* visibly highlighting what changed and why it matters;
* shortening propositions and using progressive disclosure;
* preserving the structured choices while allowing a participant to add, amend or reject an option;
* accepting free-form input and asking the user to confirm how MOSAIC has interpreted or structured it;
* showing which parts came from the user and which were suggested by the system.

These are hypotheses, not approved design changes.

### Follow-up in the remaining reader sessions

* Check whether other participants can explain the framework even when they do not remember exact stage names.
* Ask participants to identify what changed in each paired example and observe how much rereading is required.
* Ask what they wanted to enter or change when the available choices felt restrictive.
* Test whether visible difference-highlighting improves understanding without adding explanation.
* Distinguish a desire for different predefined options from a need for genuinely free-form input.
* Retain the participant’s own proposed response so it can inform a later interaction prototype.

### Current decision

Keep <issue id="43046464-d06a-4ba0-ad94-cef849fc3233" href="https://linear.app/sheridanandbairns/issue/MOS-5/run-the-first-mosaic-reader-comprehension-test">MOS-5</issue> open and gather more reader evidence. Do not redesign all examples or build unrestricted free-form interaction from this session alone. The clearest provisional design problems are comparison burden in the paired examples and constrained agency in the complete example.

## Material follow-up candidates

* Correct the false analytical lead shown when Structure + Analysis has a tie.
* Rework the complete example so that it demonstrates the richer six-stage method rather than an opaque weighted score.
* Test a clearer proposition with representative readers before undertaking a broad copy rewrite.
